$comment: Numeric policy limits for the registry. Edit here, nowhere else — tools/ and bot/ both read this file. A value with a `<name>_mirrors` sibling MUST equal the constant it names in AstraPlugins/spec/limits.yaml. tools/validate.mjs compares them for real when an AstraPlugins checkout is reachable — $ASTRA_PLUGINS_DIR, else a sibling ../AstraPlugins — and prints a `note` saying the check did not run when neither exists, because a check that quietly did not happen must not look like a check that passed.
max_artifact_bytes_note: 256 MiB, the largest .astraplugin the registry will list. Deliberately below max_extract_bytes: a bundle whose COMPRESSED size approaches the daemon's UNCOMPRESSED extraction cap cannot install.
max_index_bytes_note:
1 MiB, measured on `node tools/build-index.mjs --stdout`, which is byte-for-byte what the committed registry/v1/index.json holds before signing — both come from stableStringify, so there is no pretty-printing difference between them. .github/workflows/build-index.yml compares the deploy candidate against this number; before it did, that step echoed `wc -c` and compared it to nothing, and notes/icon-readme-contract.md's `do not let the index quietly grow past a few megabytes` was enforced by nobody reading a log line.

TODAY, measured 2026-08-22 on 10 listings: 237,384 bytes. Icons are 54.6% of it, READMEs 23.6%, and all the card text together 0.36%. READ THIS BEFORE RAISING THE NUMBER: at ~23.7 KB per listing this ceiling arrives at roughly 44 listings, on ICON growth, long before locale growth reaches it. Nine locales of card text on every listing is single-digit percent; nine locales at the schema's own caps is at most 8 KiB per listing, which is what max_listing_i18n_bytes bounds, and 100 listings all at that cap is 800 KiB and would bust this too. Both cases point at the same fix, which notes/icon-readme-contract.md already sanctions: move icon_url and readme to *_url + *_sha256 pairs. Raising this number requires a written reason here.
max_listing_i18n_bytes_note:
The whole `i18n` member of ONE listing, as UTF-8 JSON. A per-listing budget on purpose: a shared ceiling would let one verbose author stop every other author's publish behind a red catalogue build whose error names no plugin. Enforced in bot/lib/locales.mjs BEFORE the block is emitted.

IT IS A BACKSTOP, NOT A SHAPE, and the measurement says so: nine locales at the schema's own caps (64 + 200 characters) in three-byte CJK is 7,399 bytes, which is the worst case a listing can legitimately reach and sits 793 bytes under this number. What it catches is text outside the basic multilingual plane, or a per-string cap that stopped being enforced. DO NOT LOWER IT toward that 7,399: a ceiling below the legitimate worst case takes a correct CJK listing's translations away and explains it with a budget. bot/tests/ingest.test.mjs asserts the headroom in that direction.
max_locale_bytes_note: One locales/<code>.json in a bundle, checked on the raw bytes BEFORE JSON.parse. inspectBundle materialises every file the manifest lists as a Buffer bounded only by max_extract_bytes (500 MB); icons are capped at 128 KiB and READMEs at 16 KiB, and locale files were capped by nothing at all. A 200 MB flat-but-valid en.json would take the ingest runner out mid-derivation and leave the submitter's issue with no verdict — the one failure mode this bot must not have. 256 KiB is about fifty times the largest locale file in any example plugin.
max_locale_keys_note: Keys in one locale file, checked after the parse and before anything walks them. The parity rules compare key sets pairwise across every locale a bundle ships, so the work is quadratic in this number and the findings it can produce are linear in it; both are bounded here rather than discovered on a runner.
